_comment: TIER A — characters and creatures. Group file for:
uv run --project tools/art tools/art/generate.py characters --dry-run
Four entries, four billable calls, producing the art behind 150 emitted sprites
(128 carrier bodies 400..557, 16 corpses 560..575, 6 weapon glyphs 601..606) plus
the camo/glitch/hit-flash overlays that the baker derives from the carrier mask.
Every dimension below is EMITTED WIRE PIXELS AT RS=4 (ART_UPGRADE_PLAN §1).
RS=4, TileSize=6 -> TilePxR=24; BodyW/H=8/12 -> BodyWR x BodyHR = 32 x 48;
CorpseW/H = 2*TilePxR x TilePxR = 48 x 24; weapon glyph 20 x 20 (on the 20px floor).
Registration is the whole game here: code stamps fixed-position marks over the baked
blit, so the crop rect decides whether they land. Target-space anchors, derived from
render.nim bodyPixels/corpsePixels doubled from RS=2 to RS=4:
carrier 32x48 — hull top edge y=10, hull base y=36, hull x-span 4..28 (max half
width 12), crown specular y=8..9. Rows 36..47 are the code-stamped team diamond
(x 10..22, centred x=16) and MUST be empty in the generation. Rows 0..7 are the
2px bob-lift headroom (frame=1 blits at dy=-(RS div 2) = -2) plus margin.
Parity pip is stamped near x=10,y=14 — keep the left shoulder plain.
corpse 48x24 — hull y-span 6..20, hull x-span 6..38, ink top edge y=4..5, dead
visor x 12..24 / y 10..12. Rows/cols x>=38 are the code-stamped spilled diamond
(x 34..42, y 12..20) and MUST be empty in the generation. The alpha shadow pool
stays in code (the key pass binarizes alpha to 0/255, so a soft pool cannot be
generated — §3.4 step 6).
Crop rects live in art/sheets.json, hand-verified by eye against actual_px, never
here and never auto-detected (§3.3). The hard rule: crop.w/target.w == crop.h/target.h
== 2^k, k>=2. Legal rects per family are listed in each entry's notes.
Cell -> sprite index mapping (facing enum is render.nim:187, '0 S, 1 N, 2 E, 3 W'):
carrier-sheet   TL=facing 0 S, TR=facing 1 N, BL=facing 2 E, BR=facing 3 W
weapon-glyphs   TL..TR = iSword, iSpear, iBow; BL..BR = iKnives, iBlowgun, iNet
(items.nim declaration order, so ord() indexes the sheet directly)
Never mix cells across two takes of a sheet. The sheet exists to make the facings
mutually consistent; a hull from take 2 beside a hull from take 1 reintroduces exactly
the per-image drift the sheet was chosen to prevent. Pick one take whole, or re-run.

defaults.prompt_prefix:
Orthographic front view, straight on, no perspective, no camera tilt.
Single key light from the upper left. No cast shadow (the shadow is drawn separately).
Background: flat pure #00FF00, edge to edge. There must be no other green anywhere.
No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no signature.
defaults.prompt_suffix:
The subject will be composited onto a dark slate ground, RGB(40,48,57) — light it for that.

Palette, strictly:
  structure / stone / chassis  -> desaturated blue-grey, #1C242B to #4E5E6B only
  living signal / emission     -> pale cyan phosphor #A5E3EE, highlights to #EAF7FA
  matter, loot, money, energy  -> warm amber #FFB454
  contact shadow / ink line    -> near-black blue #10161C
Nothing warm except the amber. Nothing green. Nothing saturated red unless asked.

prompts.name: carrier-sheet
prompts.prompt:
A 2 by 2 grid of four views of ONE machine — the same machine four times, turned.
The whole image is a tall rectangle split into two columns and two rows, so each of
the four cells is itself a tall rectangle two units wide by three units tall. No gutter
lines, no borders, no frames, no captions, no numbering, no arrows: the cells are
separated by the flat #00FF00 background only, and each machine is centred in its cell.

Reading order, and it must be exactly this:
  top left     — the machine faced straight at the viewer, its sensor band square on
  top right    — the same machine faced directly away: no sensor band visible at all,
                 a single raised spine ridge running down the centre of its back instead
  bottom left  — the same machine turned a quarter turn to the viewer's right: the sensor
                 band slid hard against the right-hand chamfer of the upper block
  bottom right — the same machine turned a quarter turn to the viewer's left: the sensor
                 band slid hard against the left-hand chamfer of the upper block
The machine turns; the camera never does. Every cell stays a straight-on orthographic
elevation, seen level with the machine — not from above, not from below, no perspective.

The machine is a carrier: a compact, bilaterally symmetrical walking chassis. It is a
machine, not a person, not an animal, not a robot with a face — no head, no eyes, no mouth,
no arms, no legs, no feet, no wheels, no treads, no weapon, no antenna, no cables, no
hoses, no insignia. Its body is one chamfered block: vertical flanks, 45-degree cut corners
at the shoulders and again at the narrow tucked base it stands on, so the profile is
eight-sided. Hard machined edges throughout. No curves, no fillets, no rounded corners,
no circles, no spheres anywhere on it.

It is lit like a phosphor instrument, not like painted metal. Pale cyan phosphor #8ACFDC
over most of the body; #A5E3EE on the crown where the key light lands and one narrow
#EAF7FA specular strip along the top chamfer; falling to #6EB4C2 on the lit left flank,
#3E6B76 on the right flank as it turns away, and #2A4A52 under the tucked base. Across
the upper third of the body sits one recessed sensor band in near-black #10161C, and
inside that band exactly one small bright pale-cyan pupil. That band is the only thing
that differs between the four views.

All four views are identical in silhouette, proportion, size, height, width, position
within the cell and lighting direction. Do not redesign the machine between cells, do not
restyle it, do not add per-view decoration, do not change which side the light comes from.
Keep the left shoulder plain and unbusy — a mark is composited there later.

Composition inside every cell, and this is exact: the machine's bounding box is about
three quarters of the cell wide and a little over half the cell tall. Its top edge sits
about one sixth of the way down the cell; its base sits three quarters of the way down.
It is horizontally centred. The top sixth of the cell and the bottom quarter of the cell
are empty background — absolutely nothing is drawn in them: no base, no plinth, no ring,
no diamond, no ground plane, no reflection, no shadow, no glow pool.

Pixel art, drawn as if on a 128 by 192 pixel grid per cell — exactly four times the final
icon — then shown enlarged: hard-edged square blocks of flat colour, blocks aligned to the
grid, no anti-aliasing between blocks, no blur, no soft airbrushed shading, no gradient
inside a shape, no texture noise, no outer glow, no bloom, no scanlines.

Of the palette below, this image uses ONLY the blue-grey structure ramp, the pale cyan
phosphor ramp and the near-black ink. There is no amber, no magenta, no red and no team
colour anywhere in it.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 32x48 pixel icon: bold silhouette, large shapes,
no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.
prompts.notes: Phase 3 pilot. Target 32x48 per facing (BodyWR x BodyHR at RS=4). 2:3 sheet (~1365x2048) chosen over the plan's square 1024 so each 2x2 cell (~682x1024) is itself 2:3 — the model composes to the cell it sees, and the 'top sixth empty / bottom quarter empty' reservation only lands if the cell has the target's proportions. Legal crops: 512x768 (16x, expected) or 256x384 (8x) if the cells come back small; 1024x1536 (32x) will not fit a 682px column. Place each rect so the hull's top edge falls at 1/6 of the rect height and its base at 3/4 — that registration, not the rect's size, is what makes the code-stamped diamond land under the hull. Bake: --size 32x48 --ink stone --emit-mask (the mask feeds glassBodyPixels, glitchPixels and hitFlashPixels, replacing hullHalfWidth — plan risk #3).

prompts.name: corpse-wreck
prompts.prompt:
One wrecked machine, toppled onto its side, lying still and dead.

It is the same carrier chassis as the standing machine, now horizontal: one chamfered
block with vertical flanks and 45-degree cut corners, eight-sided profile, hard machined
edges, no curves, no fillets, no head, no limbs, no wheels, no weapon. It has fallen to
the viewer's left, so its sensor end lies at the left and its narrow base points right.

The wreck occupies one horizontal band exactly twice as wide as it is tall, centred in the
frame, with generous empty background above it, below it, and to the right of it. The
rightmost fifth of that band is empty background: the hull stops short of it and nothing
at all is drawn there.

The sensor band is dark and dead — a flat near-black #10161C slot near the left end with
no pupil and no light in it whatsoever.

It is cold and unpowered; nothing on it emits. Use only the dark end of the phosphor ramp,
#2A4A52 and #3E6B76, with a thin #52909D catch of the key light along the upper flank,
#1C242B to #2A3742 in the recesses, and near-black #10161C as the ink line along the top
edge. No bright cyan anywhere: no #A5E3EE, no #C6EDF4, no #EAF7FA, no glow, no bloom, no
sparks, no fire, no smoke, no blood, no gore, no organic matter. This is a dead machine,
not a body.

Damage reads as structure, not as debris: one flank plate sprung loose along a chamfer,
one corner sheared flat, the base buckled where it hit. No scattered rubble, no dust, no
loose fragments floating clear of the hull, no crater, no cast shadow and no shadow pool
beneath it — the shadow is drawn separately.

Pixel art, drawn as if on a 192 by 96 pixel grid — exactly four times the final icon —
then shown enlarged: hard-edged square blocks of flat colour, no anti-aliasing, no blur,
no soft shading, no gradient inside a shape, no texture noise, no outer glow.

Of the palette below, this image uses ONLY the blue-grey structure ramp, the dark end of
the pale cyan phosphor ramp, and the near-black ink. No amber, no magenta, no red, no
team colour.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 48x24 pixel icon: bold silhouette, large shapes,
no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.
prompts.notes: Target 48x24 (2*TilePxR x TilePxR at RS=4). 16:9 (~2048x1152) is the closest supported ratio to the 2:1 target band; the band sits centred with vertical margin. Legal crops: 1536x768 (32x, expected) or 768x384 (16x). Generate AFTER the carrier sheet is accepted and compare chassis language side by side — this is the one entry that cannot be made consistent by sheeting, so if it reads as a different machine, re-run with the accepted sheet's clauses restated, and if it still drifts, hand-topple the baked carrier instead. The prompt deliberately never says corpse, body or death: it describes a wrecked machine, which both avoids a safety block and is what AFTERGLOW actually wants (§3.5 — the grave marker is the dropped loot, not gore). Bake: --size 48x24 --ink stone.

prompts.name: weapon-glyphs
prompts.prompt:
A 3 column by 2 row grid of six flat pictogram marks, one mark centred in each of six
equal square cells. No gutter lines, no borders, no boxes, no captions, no numbering:
the cells are separated by the flat #00FF00 background only.

Reading order, and it must be exactly this:
  top row, left to right    — a sword, a spear, a bow
  bottom row, left to right — a pair of throwing knives, a blowgun, a net

Every mark is a single flat fill of pale cyan phosphor #A5E3EE and nothing else: no
outline, no interior shading, no highlight, no second colour, no gradient, no depth, no
perspective, no material, no wood, no steel. Flat silhouettes on the background.

Draw them as machined pictograms, not illustrations, and keep them one family: every
stroke is a straight segment, horizontal, vertical or at 45 degrees; corners are cut
square or chamfered; no smooth curves anywhere; all six share the same diagonal.
  sword    — a broad straight blade on a 45-degree diagonal running up to the right, a
             plain crossbar at its base, a short square grip below the crossbar
  spear    — one long straight shaft on the same diagonal, clearly narrower than the
             sword and clearly longer, ending in a solid triangular head, no crossbar
  bow      — an upright bow drawn as three straight chamfered segments meeting at blunt
             angles instead of a smooth arc, a straight taut string across the chord, one
             nocked arrow crossing it horizontally
  knives   — two short straight blades crossed in an X, each with a small square pommel
             at its butt end
  blowgun  — one long straight tube on a shallow, nearly horizontal diagonal, a square
             flared mouthpiece at its lower left end, one small detached dart just beyond
             the muzzle
  net      — a diamond-shaped lattice of crossing straight cords with a square weight at
             each of its four outer points

The six must be told apart by outline alone, at a glance, at thumbnail size: no two
silhouettes may read the same. Each mark fills about four fifths of its cell and is
centred in it.

Strokes are thick and blunt: no stroke narrower than one eighth of the cell width, and no
gap between two strokes narrower than that either. Nothing tapers to a point thinner than
one eighth of the cell.

Pixel art, drawn as if on a 40 by 40 pixel grid per cell — exactly twice the final icon —
then shown enlarged: hard-edged square blocks of flat colour, no anti-aliasing, no blur,
no soft shading, no texture noise, no outer glow.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 20x20 pixel icon: bold silhouette, large shapes,
no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.
prompts.notes: Target 20x20 each — exactly on the plan's 20px Tier A floor, so treat the generation as a TRACING REFERENCE, not a downsample source (§2 caveat). 3:2 (~2048x1365) gives six square ~682px cells for a 3x2 grid. Legal crops: 640x640 (32x, expected — a 320x320 rect would clip a mark drawn at 4/5 of a 682px cell) or 320x320 (16x) only if the model returns small cells and the whole mark fits inside. Flat single-value marks survive a 32x box reduction cleanly (coverage-weighted edge, then ramp snap). Held weapons are PHOSPHOR, not amber: amber is matter/economy and belongs to the ground chip, while the held glyph is live signal on a living agent (§3.1 law 3, §3.3 'weapon read'). This also kills the last green in the build, the (120,160,110) blowgun. Bake: --size 20x20 --palette phosphor --ink none.

prompts.name: camo-shimmer-plate
prompts.prompt:
One flat plate of faceted refractive glass, seen straight on, filling and over-filling the
whole composition. The plate's own edges run past the framing on all four sides, so no edge
of the plate is visible and no background is visible either — the plate IS the background,
edge to edge. It covers the frame completely, so there is nothing for the key colour to key
and no #00FF00 should appear anywhere in this one image.

The material is broken into large flat facets, like a cracked pane or a rough-cut crystal
seen face on: straight-edged shards meeting at hard angles, each facet somewhere between
one sixth and one third of the frame width across, each facet a single plain unshaded fill,
no two adjacent facets the same value. A few facet boundaries catch the upper-left key light
as a bright straight sliver of #C6EDF4 or #EAF7FA; every other facet stays in the dark end
of the phosphor ramp, #2A4A52 through #52909D, with #1C242B in the deepest facets.

It is a material swatch, not an object: no subject, no figure, no silhouette, no machine,
no border, no frame, no vignette, no corner darkening, no repeating tile pattern, no visible
seams, no lens flare, no bloom, no blur, no gradient, no anti-aliasing, no caustics.

Pixel art, drawn as if on a 128 by 192 pixel grid — exactly four times the final icon —
then shown enlarged: hard-edged square blocks of flat colour.

Of the palette below, this image uses ONLY the pale cyan phosphor ramp and the darkest
blue-greys. No amber, no magenta, no red, no team colour.

Designed to stay legible when reduced to a 32x48 pixel icon: bold silhouette, large shapes,
no fine detail, no thin lines under 1/12 of the sprite width.
prompts.notes: OPTIONAL and OUT OF THE 36-IMAGE BUDGET. The plan puts camo/glitch/hit-flash in Tier B at ZERO images: all three are derived from the baked carrier's alpha mask, because an independently generated silhouette guarantees misregistration (risk #3). This entry does not violate that — it generates a MATERIAL, never a silhouette. The baker masks it with CarrierPose[facing].mask and glassBodyPixels applies its own alpha (rim 96 / fill 30) exactly as today, so registration still comes from the mask and the baked plate stays opaque (0/255 alpha, keeping the §3.4 step-6 histogram assertion valid). Generate only if the mask-derived camo reads as a flat wash at 1:1; the fallback is the pure-code derivation and nothing else changes. The full-bleed instruction contradicts the group prefix's 'background: flat pure #00FF00' on purpose, and harmlessly: if the model surrounds the plate with green anyway, the hand-verified crop takes an interior rect and the surround never reaches the baker. Crop an INTERIOR rect only, never one containing the plate's own edge: 1024x1536 (32x, expected) or 512x768 (16x). Bake: --size 32x48 --palette phosphor --ink none.
